title: Triton — Trellis implementation daylog
content:
Triton — Trellis implementation daylog (working notes)
Owner: Maya Chen | SE lead for Trellis POC
Goal: get Redwood Private (VPC) demo-ready for Trellis pilot, validate model pinning + fallback routing, confirm throughput SLO with their batch job.

Quick context
- Customer: Trellis Health (mid-market, US + EU users, HIPAA scope).
- POC targets: 50 rps peak, 95th latency < 1200ms, token cost baseline using mix of Llama-3-8B and quantized Llama-3-4bit variant.
- Must demonstrate: VPC peering, KMS integration, model version pin + canary rollback, and audit log ingestion to their SIEM.

Today (2026-03-05)
- Morning stand w/ Ravi & Evelyn: confirmed VPC CIDR ranges and allowed subnets for peering (see notes below).
- Spent 1.5h on Private control plane onboarding; hit issue with DNS resolution across peered VPCs.
- Got around with temporary hosts file in bastion to continue. Need permanent fix: update customer route table and Dropbox of DNS forwarding rules.

Outstanding blocking items
1) DNS forwarding for redwood-private-controlplane.internal -> must be reachable from customer app subnet.
   - Action: Ravi to open ticket with infra (WAN-DNS) + Trellis infra contact (A. Gomez). ETA 2026-03-07.
2) KMS policy scope: Trellis uses customer-managed KMS in eu-west-1. We need decrypt IAM role mapping for control plane.
   - Action: Maya to share IAM trust doc + sample policy. (MAYA-TO-DO)
3) Audit log sink to Splunk (their SIEM) via s3 -> lambda forwarding. We need an example ingestion pipeline.
   - Action: Evelyn to draft Splunk ingestion steps and test with sample logs.

Notes / config snippets (for quick paste)
- VPC peering summary (agreed)
  - Trellis VPC: 10.20.0.0/16 (nat-subnet: 10.20.1.0/24)
  - Redwood Private VPC: 10.50.0.0/16
  - Allowed routes: 10.20.0.0/16 -> peering (propogate to control plane ELBs)

- Example IAM KMS policy (customer needs to attach):
  {
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDCUST:role/redwood-controlplane"},
        "Action": ["kms:Encrypt", "kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey"],
        "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:REDCUST:key/EXAMPLE-KEY-ID"
      }
    ]
  }
  - Note: replace REDCUST with Trellis account ID. Customer asked for minimal privileges; map only to role ARN we exchange in onboarding doc.

- Control plane DNS workaround used earlier:
  - On bastion: echo '10.50.2.12 redwood-controlplane.internal' >> /etc/hosts
  - Temporary only — do not keep in final instructions.

Model pinning & rollout plan (short)
- Start with model: llama-3-8b:redwood-v1 (baseline). Canary: llama-3-8b:redwood-v1-quantized (lower cost).
- Route policy: 5% traffic to canary first 2 hours -> 25% next day if errors <= 0.5% and P95 < baseline * 1.2
- Fallback: if errors > 2% in 10m, automatic rollback to baseline (control plane policy).
- Prompt quality validation: sample prompt set (see linked PR) to be run nightly via Redwood Optimize eval job.

Perf test plan (to run after networking fixes)
1) Load harness: use wrk2 with 50 concurrent connections -> ramp to 60 rps for 15m. Capture token/tps and p95 latency.
2) Batching config: try batch_max_tokens 2048, max_batch_size 16; measure tail latencies.
3) KV cache: enable prefix caching for session-type requests; track cache hit rate.

Temporary checklist (today)
- [x] Confirm VPC ranges w/ Trellis (done)
- [x] Create initial control-plane invite + onboarding link (done)
- [ ] Resolve DNS forwarding (blocking)
- [ ] Send IAM KMS sample policy to Trellis (Maya)
- [ ] Create Splunk ingestion sample (Evelyn)
- [ ] Schedule perf run once DNS fixed (Ravi)

Meeting notes snippets
- Trellis product asked to avoid public egress for any PHI payloads. Confirmed we can keep egress within VPC and use dedicated NATs. Need to ensure logs redact PHI before sending to Splunk.
- Compliance ask: 90 day audit log retention for POC. We agreed to 90 days on S3 lifecycle rule.

Small technical checklist (commands / useful links)
- Check control plane reachability: curl -v https://controlplane.redwood.internal/health --resolve 'controlplane.redwood.internal:443:10.50.2.12'
- List model variants: redwoodctl models list --env private --customer trellis
- Pin model: redwoodctl rollout create --customer trellis --route default --model llama-3-8b:redwood-v1 --strategy pinned

Questions to clarify with Trellis (before next demo)
- Confirm whether they require dedicated HSM or CMAK-backed keys for KMS usage.
- Exact Splunk ingest endpoint and any firewall allowlist IPs for Lambda -> Splunk.
- Will Trellis want per-tenant routing (multi-tenant inside their VPC) or single shared endpoint? Impacts SNI and cert setup.

Next steps (by 2026-03-07)
- Ravi: open infra ticket for DNS + update route tables.
- Maya: send KMS IAM sample + onboarding checklist to Trellis security.
- Evelyn: prototype Splunk ingestion and push sample logs.
- All: quick sync Friday 10:30 PT to review perf test readiness.

Random notes / friction log (quick capture)
- Control plane health endpoint returns 502 sometimes when we hit session cache flush — track with tracing ID on next run.
- Consider enabling graceful backoff policy in edge router to reduce 502 spikes when KV cache recirculation occurs.

End of daylog. Keep this file as working scratchpad; push finalized steps into Confluence after DNS + KMS items resolved.

-- Maya
